findings.text: — s16's Why and done-when rest on the quoted line `missing baseline_suite.command_matches_suite_command, after_suite.command_matches_suite_command` being what a trailing after-suite revision produces today, but `_arm_matches`-side comparison (`reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:715-720`) accepts the command resolved at the arm's own recorded revision — `_scoped_suite_command(record, revision=revision)` — so a revision alone does not raise `command_matches_suite_command`; the baseline arm's revision is separately compared to `base_sha` at `:797-803` as `baseline_suite.revision_matches_base_sha`, and no after-side revision check exists. The defect is real and worth landing, but the evidence quoted for it is §14's (ordering and interpreter spelling), and s16's done-when claim that at the base revision such a manifest "is refused only with the bare line" is therefore likely false — it is probably accepted outright. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: the worker would run the base reproduction, find no refusal, and either report a blocker or write a test asserting a behaviour the plan mis-describes; correcting the Why to "today an after arm at a trailing revision is accepted when its command matches at that revision" and the done-when's first line to show the acceptance makes the reproduction showable.

— s15 declares one negative control, "drops the revisions from the brief", which reddens only case one; case two asserts that a composed resume `advice` names both revisions with two different resolved commands, and no control makes the advice composer fail. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: the advice composer is a second surface in a different module (`reckon/crew/resumption.py`), and without a control the node's only evidence for it is a test that passes on any implementation; adding a second control that drops the revisions from the advice, which must redden case two, is what makes that half of the section falsifiable.
